opening.argument: The presentation identifies itself as a Polkadot bootcamp lesson on the basic fundamentals of blockchain programming. It explicitly frames the session as instruction, beginning with “hello welcome back to the bootcamp today we're going to restart on W2 to learning about the basic fundamentals of blockchain programming.” The material then explains blockchain as “a decentralized public ledger” whose blocks store verified transactions, and the slides cover blocks, transactions, hashes, nodes, validators, and consensus mechanisms. Although it mentions financial applications and blockchain networks, it contains no request for payment, credentials, investment, or other financial participation. The evidence therefore supports an educational technology lesson, without establishing a solicitation or promised financial outcome.
